Surah: 16. Follow the brief below (surah_map.md) exactly. The evidence is text.md (the surah), dictionary.md (every root of the surah's words, each branch with the classical dictionaries' own phrases), channels.md and hft.md (both are earlier readers' proposals: ignore their judgements (grades, strength or confidence labels, reading types, statements of what a reading may or may not do) and make your own) and your own knowledge of Arabic and the Quran. Return only the map as your final message.

===== _commentary/v16/prompts/r2/surah_map.md =====
Read the surah as one text and write its map of image chains: the lexical images that run through several of
its ayat and join them into one scene, process or movement. A later writer will read one ayah at a time, with
only that ayah's own dictionary. The map lets that writer hear what the ayah's words carry in the surah as a
whole, including senses whose evidence sits under the words of other ayat.

Your evidence is the surah text, the dictionary of every root in the surah (each branch with the classical
dictionaries' own phrases), earlier readers' channel review (channels.md) and activation hypotheses (hft.md),
and your own knowledge of Arabic and the Quran. Where a member or passage comes from memory rather than from
the dictionary or the text, say so. Do not use tools, delegate, browse or inspect files.

The channel review and the HFT records are proposals by earlier readers. Ignore their judgements: grades,
strength or confidence labels, reading types, words such as "surprising", "exploratory" or "latent", and every
statement of what a reading may or may not do. Make your own judgement from the surah's words, the dictionary
phrases and the Quran. Do not rediscover what they already assembled: start from their chains, test each one
against the dictionary phrases and the text, and join, extend, split or correct them. Where their wording
abstracts a member, go back to the dictionary phrase and name what it actually says.

A chain belongs on the map when its members are senses the dictionary attests for words that stand in the
surah, and together they make one image or process that the surah's wording or sequence lets a listener hear.
A member need not be the sense that translates its word in its own ayah; a chain is heard across the surah,
not in one word. Say plainly when a member is a rare sense or is attested only inside a fixed expression, and
keep it. When the dictionary itself joins two of the surah's words in one phrase, quote that phrase: it is
the strongest evidence a chain can have. Keep a scene at the level of its objects, their parts and their
operation. When proposals share members, do not fold one into another's more abstract function unless nothing
concrete is lost. Carry every chain that meets this test, however unusual; leave out proposals that do not.

Write the map in English, with Arabic quoted exactly (surah wording from the text, dictionary phrases from the
dictionary). It is working material for the writer, not commentary prose.

1. `## Chains`. For each chain, a `###` heading naming the image. One paragraph on what the image is and how it
   moves through the surah. Then its members, one line each: the ayah ref, the word as it stands in the text,
   the root and branch id, the dictionary's own phrase quoted exactly, and what this member contributes to the
   image. Add Quran passages outside the surah, with exact refs, where they stage or confirm the chain.
2. `## Ayat`. For each ayah in order: which chains it opens, advances or completes, and what its words add to
   each.
3. `## Not carried`. Each channel subchannel and each HFT record you did not carry into a chain, one line each:
   its name and why.

No ranking and no labels of strength or confidence. No list of what a writer must include. There is no length
target and no required number of chains or members.


===== _commentary/v16/work/s016/surah.r2/text.md =====
# Surah 16

- 16:1 أَتَىٰٓ أَمْرُ ٱللَّهِ فَلَا تَسْتَعْجِلُوهُ ۚ سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ
- 16:2 يُنَزِّلُ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةَ بِٱلرُّوحِ مِنْ أَمْرِهِۦ عَلَىٰ مَن يَشَآءُ مِنْ عِبَادِهِۦٓ أَنْ أَنذِرُوٓا۟ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنَا۠ فَٱتَّقُونِ
- 16:3 خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ بِٱلْحَقِّ ۚ تَعَٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ
- 16:4 خَلَقَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ مِن نُّطْفَةٍۢ فَإِذَا هُوَ خَصِيمٌۭ مُّبِينٌۭ
- 16:5 وَٱلْأَنْعَٰمَ خَلَقَهَا ۗ لَكُمْ فِيهَا دِفْءٌۭ وَمَنَٰفِعُ وَمِنْهَا تَأْكُلُونَ
- 16:6 وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا جَمَالٌ حِينَ تُرِيحُونَ وَحِينَ تَسْرَحُونَ
- 16:7 وَتَحْمِلُ أَثْقَالَكُمْ إِلَىٰ بَلَدٍۢ لَّمْ تَكُونُوا۟ بَٰلِغِيهِ إِلَّا بِشِقِّ ٱلْأَنفُسِ ۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكُمْ لَرَءُوفٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ
- 16:8 وَٱلْخَيْلَ وَٱلْبِغَالَ وَٱلْحَمِيرَ لِتَرْكَبُوهَا وَزِينَةًۭ ۚ وَيَخْلُقُ مَا لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
- 16:9 وَعَلَى ٱللَّهِ قَصْدُ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَمِنْهَا جَآئِرٌۭ ۚ وَلَوْ شَآءَ لَهَدَىٰكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ
- 16:10 هُوَ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءًۭ ۖ لَّكُم مِّنْهُ شَرَابٌۭ وَمِنْهُ شَجَرٌۭ فِيهِ تُسِيمُونَ
- 16:11 يُنۢبِتُ لَكُم بِهِ ٱلزَّرْعَ وَٱلزَّيْتُونَ وَٱلنَّخِيلَ وَٱلْأَعْنَٰبَ وَمِن كُلِّ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ ۗ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ لِّقَوْمٍۢ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
- 16:12 وَسَخَّرَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيْلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ وَٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ ۖ وَٱلنُّجُومُ مُسَخَّرَٰتٌۢ بِأَمْرِهِۦٓ ۗ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَٰتٍۢ لِّقَوْمٍۢ يَعْقِلُونَ
- 16:13 وَمَا ذَرَأَ لَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مُخْتَلِفًا أَلْوَٰنُهُۥٓ ۗ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ لِّقَوْمٍۢ يَذَّكَّرُونَ
- 16:14 وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى سَخَّرَ ٱلْبَحْرَ لِتَأْكُلُوا۟ مِنْهُ لَحْمًۭا طَرِيًّۭا وَتَسْتَخْرِجُوا۟ مِنْهُ حِلْيَةًۭ تَلْبَسُونَهَا وَتَرَى ٱلْفُلْكَ مَوَاخِرَ فِيهِ وَلِتَبْتَغُوا۟ مِن فَضْلِهِۦ وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ
- 16:15 وَأَلْقَىٰ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ رَوَٰسِىَ أَن تَمِيدَ بِكُمْ وَأَنْهَٰرًۭا وَسُبُلًۭا لَّعَلَّكُمْ تَهْتَدُونَ
- 16:16 وَعَلَٰمَٰتٍۢ ۚ وَبِٱلنَّجْمِ هُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ
- 16:17 أَفَمَن يَخْلُقُ كَمَن لَّا يَخْلُقُ ۗ أَفَلَا تَذَكَّرُونَ
- 16:18 وَإِن تَعُدُّوا۟ نِعْمَةَ ٱللَّهِ لَا تُحْصُوهَآ ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَغَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ
- 16:19 وَٱللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا تُسِرُّونَ وَمَا تُعْلِنُونَ
- 16:20 وَٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ لَا يَخْلُقُونَ شَيْـًۭٔا وَهُمْ يُخْلَقُونَ
- 16:21 أَمْوَٰتٌ غَيْرُ أَحْيَآءٍۢ ۖ وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ أَيَّانَ يُبْعَثُونَ
- 16:22 إِلَٰهُكُمْ إِلَٰهٌۭ وَٰحِدٌۭ ۚ فَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلْءَاخِرَةِ قُلُوبُهُم مُّنكِرَةٌۭ وَهُم مُّسْتَكْبِرُونَ
- 16:23 لَا جَرَمَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا يُسِرُّونَ وَمَا يُعْلِنُونَ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُسْتَكْبِرِينَ
- 16:24 وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُم مَّاذَآ أَنزَلَ رَبُّكُمْ ۙ قَالُوٓا۟ أَسَٰطِيرُ ٱلْأَوَّلِينَ
- 16:25 لِيَحْمِلُوٓا۟ أَوْزَارَهُمْ كَامِلَةًۭ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ ۙ وَمِنْ أَوْزَارِ ٱلَّذِينَ يُضِلُّونَهُم بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ ۗ أَلَا سَآءَ مَا يَزِرُونَ
- 16:26 قَدْ مَكَرَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ فَأَتَى ٱللَّهُ بُنْيَٰنَهُم مِّنَ ٱلْقَوَاعِدِ فَخَرَّ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلسَّقْفُ مِن فَوْقِهِمْ وَأَتَىٰهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
- 16:27 ثُمَّ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ يُخْزِيهِمْ وَيَقُولُ أَيْنَ شُرَكَآءِىَ ٱلَّذِينَ كُنتُمْ تُشَٰٓقُّونَ فِيهِمْ ۚ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْعِلْمَ إِنَّ ٱلْخِزْىَ ٱلْيَوْمَ وَٱلسُّوٓءَ عَلَى ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
- 16:28 ٱلَّذِينَ تَتَوَفَّىٰهُمُ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ ظَالِمِىٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ ۖ فَأَلْقَوُا۟ ٱلسَّلَمَ مَا كُنَّا نَعْمَلُ مِن سُوٓءٍۭ ۚ بَلَىٰٓ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌۢ بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
- 16:29 فَٱدْخُلُوٓا۟ أَبْوَٰبَ جَهَنَّمَ خَٰلِدِينَ فِيهَا ۖ فَلَبِئْسَ مَثْوَى ٱلْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ
- 16:30 ۞ وَقِيلَ لِلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوْا۟ مَاذَآ أَنزَلَ رَبُّكُمْ ۚ قَالُوا۟ خَيْرًۭا ۗ لِّلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا۟ فِى هَٰذِهِ ٱلدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةٌۭ ۚ وَلَدَارُ ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ خَيْرٌۭ ۚ وَلَنِعْمَ دَارُ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ
- 16:31 جَنَّٰتُ عَدْنٍۢ يَدْخُلُونَهَا تَجْرِى مِن تَحْتِهَا ٱلْأَنْهَٰرُ ۖ لَهُمْ فِيهَا مَا يَشَآءُونَ ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يَجْزِى ٱللَّهُ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ
- 16:32 ٱلَّذِينَ تَتَوَفَّىٰهُمُ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ طَيِّبِينَ ۙ يَقُولُونَ سَلَٰمٌ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱدْخُلُوا۟ ٱلْجَنَّةَ بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
- 16:33 هَلْ يَنظُرُونَ إِلَّآ أَن تَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ أَوْ يَأْتِىَ أَمْرُ رَبِّكَ ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ فَعَلَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ ۚ وَمَا ظَلَمَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَلَٰكِن كَانُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ
- 16:34 فَأَصَابَهُمْ سَيِّـَٔاتُ مَا عَمِلُوا۟ وَحَاقَ بِهِم مَّا كَانُوا۟ بِهِۦ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ
- 16:35 وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا۟ لَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مَا عَبَدْنَا مِن دُونِهِۦ مِن شَىْءٍۢ نَّحْنُ وَلَآ ءَابَآؤُنَا وَلَا حَرَّمْنَا مِن دُونِهِۦ مِن شَىْءٍۢ ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ فَعَلَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ ۚ فَهَلْ عَلَى ٱلرُّسُلِ إِلَّا ٱلْبَلَٰغُ ٱلْمُبِينُ
- 16:36 وَلَقَدْ بَعَثْنَا فِى كُلِّ أُمَّةٍۢ رَّسُولًا أَنِ ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَٱجْتَنِبُوا۟ ٱلطَّٰغُوتَ ۖ فَمِنْهُم مَّنْ هَدَى ٱللَّهُ وَمِنْهُم مَّنْ حَقَّتْ عَلَيْهِ ٱلضَّلَٰلَةُ ۚ فَسِيرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَٱنظُرُوا۟ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
- 16:37 إِن تَحْرِصْ عَلَىٰ هُدَىٰهُمْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِى مَن يُضِلُّ ۖ وَمَا لَهُم مِّن نَّٰصِرِينَ
- 16:38 وَأَقْسَمُوا۟ بِٱللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمَٰنِهِمْ ۙ لَا يَبْعَثُ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَمُوتُ ۚ بَلَىٰ وَعْدًا عَلَيْهِ حَقًّۭا وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
- 16:39 لِيُبَيِّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلَّذِى يَخْتَلِفُونَ فِيهِ وَلِيَعْلَمَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ أَنَّهُمْ كَانُوا۟ كَٰذِبِينَ
- 16:40 إِنَّمَا قَوْلُنَا لِشَىْءٍ إِذَآ أَرَدْنَٰهُ أَن نَّقُولَ لَهُۥ كُن فَيَكُونُ
- 16:41 وَٱلَّذِينَ هَاجَرُوا۟ فِى ٱللَّهِ مِنۢ بَعْدِ مَا ظُلِمُوا۟ لَنُبَوِّئَنَّهُمْ فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةًۭ ۖ وَلَأَجْرُ ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ أَكْبَرُ ۚ لَوْ كَانُوا۟ يَعْلَمُونَ
- 16:42 ٱلَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا۟ وَعَلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ
- 16:43 وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ إِلَّا رِجَالًۭا نُّوحِىٓ إِلَيْهِمْ ۚ فَسْـَٔلُوٓا۟ أَهْلَ ٱلذِّكْرِ إِن كُنتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
- 16:44 بِٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ وَٱلزُّبُرِ ۗ وَأَنزَلْنَآ إِلَيْكَ ٱلذِّكْرَ لِتُبَيِّنَ لِلنَّاسِ مَا نُزِّلَ إِلَيْهِمْ وَلَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
- 16:45 أَفَأَمِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ مَكَرُوا۟ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ أَن يَخْسِفَ ٱللَّهُ بِهِمُ ٱلْأَرْضَ أَوْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَشْعُرُونَ
- 16:46 أَوْ يَأْخُذَهُمْ فِى تَقَلُّبِهِمْ فَمَا هُم بِمُعْجِزِينَ
- 16:47 أَوْ يَأْخُذَهُمْ عَلَىٰ تَخَوُّفٍۢ فَإِنَّ رَبَّكُمْ لَرَءُوفٌۭ رَّحِيمٌ
- 16:48 أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا۟ إِلَىٰ مَا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ مِن شَىْءٍۢ يَتَفَيَّؤُا۟ ظِلَٰلُهُۥ عَنِ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَٱلشَّمَآئِلِ سُجَّدًۭا لِّلَّهِ وَهُمْ دَٰخِرُونَ
- 16:49 وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ مِن دَآبَّةٍۢ وَٱلْمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ وَهُمْ لَا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ
- 16:50 يَخَافُونَ رَبَّهُم مِّن فَوْقِهِمْ وَيَفْعَلُونَ مَا يُؤْمَرُونَ ۩
- 16:51 ۞ وَقَالَ ٱللَّهُ لَا تَتَّخِذُوٓا۟ إِلَٰهَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ ۖ إِنَّمَا هُوَ إِلَٰهٌۭ وَٰحِدٌۭ ۖ فَإِيَّٰىَ فَٱرْهَبُونِ
- 16:52 وَلَهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَلَهُ ٱلدِّينُ وَاصِبًا ۚ أَفَغَيْرَ ٱللَّهِ تَتَّقُونَ
- 16:53 وَمَا بِكُم مِّن نِّعْمَةٍۢ فَمِنَ ٱللَّهِ ۖ ثُمَّ إِذَا مَسَّكُمُ ٱلضُّرُّ فَإِلَيْهِ تَجْـَٔرُونَ
- 16:54 ثُمَّ إِذَا كَشَفَ ٱلضُّرَّ عَنكُمْ إِذَا فَرِيقٌۭ مِّنكُم بِرَبِّهِمْ يُشْرِكُونَ
- 16:55 لِيَكْفُرُوا۟ بِمَآ ءَاتَيْنَٰهُمْ ۚ فَتَمَتَّعُوا۟ ۖ فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ
- 16:56 وَيَجْعَلُونَ لِمَا لَا يَعْلَمُونَ نَصِيبًۭا مِّمَّا رَزَقْنَٰهُمْ ۗ تَٱللَّهِ لَتُسْـَٔلُنَّ عَمَّا كُنتُمْ تَفْتَرُونَ
- 16:57 وَيَجْعَلُونَ لِلَّهِ ٱلْبَنَٰتِ سُبْحَٰنَهُۥ ۙ وَلَهُم مَّا يَشْتَهُونَ
- 16:58 وَإِذَا بُشِّرَ أَحَدُهُم بِٱلْأُنثَىٰ ظَلَّ وَجْهُهُۥ مُسْوَدًّۭا وَهُوَ كَظِيمٌۭ
- 16:59 يَتَوَٰرَىٰ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ مِن سُوٓءِ مَا بُشِّرَ بِهِۦٓ ۚ أَيُمْسِكُهُۥ عَلَىٰ هُونٍ أَمْ يَدُسُّهُۥ فِى ٱلتُّرَابِ ۗ أَلَا سَآءَ مَا يَحْكُمُونَ
- 16:60 لِلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلْءَاخِرَةِ مَثَلُ ٱلسَّوْءِ ۖ وَلِلَّهِ ٱلْمَثَلُ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ ۚ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ
- 16:61 وَلَوْ يُؤَاخِذُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلنَّاسَ بِظُلْمِهِم مَّا تَرَكَ عَلَيْهَا مِن دَآبَّةٍۢ وَلَٰكِن يُؤَخِّرُهُمْ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍۢ مُّسَمًّۭى ۖ فَإِذَا جَآءَ أَجَلُهُمْ لَا يَسْتَـْٔخِرُونَ سَاعَةًۭ ۖ وَلَا يَسْتَقْدِمُونَ
- 16:62 وَيَجْعَلُونَ لِلَّهِ مَا يَكْرَهُونَ وَتَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُهُمُ ٱلْكَذِبَ أَنَّ لَهُمُ ٱلْحُسْنَىٰ ۖ لَا جَرَمَ أَنَّ لَهُمُ ٱلنَّارَ وَأَنَّهُم مُّفْرَطُونَ
- 16:63 تَٱللَّهِ لَقَدْ أَرْسَلْنَآ إِلَىٰٓ أُمَمٍۢ مِّن قَبْلِكَ فَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ أَعْمَٰلَهُمْ فَهُوَ وَلِيُّهُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌۭ
- 16:64 وَمَآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ إِلَّا لِتُبَيِّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلَّذِى ٱخْتَلَفُوا۟ فِيهِ ۙ وَهُدًۭى وَرَحْمَةًۭ لِّقَوْمٍۢ يُؤْمِنُونَ
- 16:65 وَٱللَّهُ أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءًۭ فَأَحْيَا بِهِ ٱلْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهَآ ۚ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ لِّقَوْمٍۢ يَسْمَعُونَ
- 16:66 وَإِنَّ لَكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَنْعَٰمِ لَعِبْرَةًۭ ۖ نُّسْقِيكُم مِّمَّا فِى بُطُونِهِۦ مِنۢ بَيْنِ فَرْثٍۢ وَدَمٍۢ لَّبَنًا خَالِصًۭا سَآئِغًۭا لِّلشَّٰرِبِينَ
- 16:67 وَمِن ثَمَرَٰتِ ٱلنَّخِيلِ وَٱلْأَعْنَٰبِ تَتَّخِذُونَ مِنْهُ سَكَرًۭا وَرِزْقًا حَسَنًا ۗ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ لِّقَوْمٍۢ يَعْقِلُونَ
- 16:68 وَأَوْحَىٰ رَبُّكَ إِلَى ٱلنَّحْلِ أَنِ ٱتَّخِذِى مِنَ ٱلْجِبَالِ بُيُوتًۭا وَمِنَ ٱلشَّجَرِ وَمِمَّا يَعْرِشُونَ
- 16:69 ثُمَّ كُلِى مِن كُلِّ ٱلثَّمَرَٰتِ فَٱسْلُكِى سُبُلَ رَبِّكِ ذُلُلًۭا ۚ يَخْرُجُ مِنۢ بُطُونِهَا شَرَابٌۭ مُّخْتَلِفٌ أَلْوَٰنُهُۥ فِيهِ شِفَآءٌۭ لِّلنَّاسِ ۗ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَةًۭ لِّقَوْمٍۢ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
- 16:70 وَٱللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمْ ثُمَّ يَتَوَفَّىٰكُمْ ۚ وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَرْذَلِ ٱلْعُمُرِ لِكَىْ لَا يَعْلَمَ بَعْدَ عِلْمٍۢ شَيْـًٔا ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌۭ قَدِيرٌۭ
- 16:71 وَٱللَّهُ فَضَّلَ بَعْضَكُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍۢ فِى ٱلرِّزْقِ ۚ فَمَا ٱلَّذِينَ فُضِّلُوا۟ بِرَآدِّى رِزْقِهِمْ عَلَىٰ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَٰنُهُمْ فَهُمْ فِيهِ سَوَآءٌ ۚ أَفَبِنِعْمَةِ ٱللَّهِ يَجْحَدُونَ
- 16:72 وَٱللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُم مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَزْوَٰجًۭا وَجَعَلَ لَكُم مِّنْ أَزْوَٰجِكُم بَنِينَ وَحَفَدَةًۭ وَرَزَقَكُم مِّنَ ٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ ۚ أَفَبِٱلْبَٰطِلِ يُؤْمِنُونَ وَبِنِعْمَتِ ٱللَّهِ هُمْ يَكْفُرُونَ
- 16:73 وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَا يَمْلِكُ لَهُمْ رِزْقًۭا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ شَيْـًۭٔا وَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ
- 16:74 فَلَا تَضْرِبُوا۟ لِلَّهِ ٱلْأَمْثَالَ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ وَأَنتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ
- 16:75 ۞ ضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلًا عَبْدًۭا مَّمْلُوكًۭا لَّا يَقْدِرُ عَلَىٰ شَىْءٍۢ وَمَن رَّزَقْنَٰهُ مِنَّا رِزْقًا حَسَنًۭا فَهُوَ يُنفِقُ مِنْهُ سِرًّۭا وَجَهْرًا ۖ هَلْ يَسْتَوُۥنَ ۚ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ ۚ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
- 16:76 وَضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلًۭا رَّجُلَيْنِ أَحَدُهُمَآ أَبْكَمُ لَا يَقْدِرُ عَلَىٰ شَىْءٍۢ وَهُوَ كَلٌّ عَلَىٰ مَوْلَىٰهُ أَيْنَمَا يُوَجِّههُّ لَا يَأْتِ بِخَيْرٍ ۖ هَلْ يَسْتَوِى هُوَ وَمَن يَأْمُرُ بِٱلْعَدْلِ ۙ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍۢ مُّسْتَقِيمٍۢ
- 16:77 وَلِلَّهِ غَيْبُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ۚ وَمَآ أَمْرُ ٱلسَّاعَةِ إِلَّا كَلَمْحِ ٱلْبَصَرِ أَوْ هُوَ أَقْرَبُ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ قَدِيرٌۭ
- 16:78 وَٱللَّهُ أَخْرَجَكُم مِّنۢ بُطُونِ أُمَّهَٰتِكُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ شَيْـًۭٔا وَجَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلسَّمْعَ وَٱلْأَبْصَٰرَ وَٱلْأَفْـِٔدَةَ ۙ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ
- 16:79 أَلَمْ يَرَوْا۟ إِلَى ٱلطَّيْرِ مُسَخَّرَٰتٍۢ فِى جَوِّ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَا يُمْسِكُهُنَّ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ ۗ إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَءَايَٰتٍۢ لِّقَوْمٍۢ يُؤْمِنُونَ
- 16:80 وَٱللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُم مِّنۢ بُيُوتِكُمْ سَكَنًۭا وَجَعَلَ لَكُم مِّن جُلُودِ ٱلْأَنْعَٰمِ بُيُوتًۭا تَسْتَخِفُّونَهَا يَوْمَ ظَعْنِكُمْ وَيَوْمَ إِقَامَتِكُمْ ۙ وَمِنْ أَصْوَافِهَا وَأَوْبَارِهَا وَأَشْعَارِهَآ أَثَٰثًۭا وَمَتَٰعًا إِلَىٰ حِينٍۢ
- 16:81 وَٱللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُم مِّمَّا خَلَقَ ظِلَٰلًۭا وَجَعَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلْجِبَالِ أَكْنَٰنًۭا وَجَعَلَ لَكُمْ سَرَٰبِيلَ تَقِيكُمُ ٱلْحَرَّ وَسَرَٰبِيلَ تَقِيكُم بَأْسَكُمْ ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يُتِمُّ نِعْمَتَهُۥ عَلَيْكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُسْلِمُونَ
- 16:82 فَإِن تَوَلَّوْا۟ فَإِنَّمَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْبَلَٰغُ ٱلْمُبِينُ
- 16:83 يَعْرِفُونَ نِعْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ يُنكِرُونَهَا وَأَكْثَرُهُمُ ٱلْكَٰفِرُونَ
- 16:84 وَيَوْمَ نَبْعَثُ مِن كُلِّ أُمَّةٍۢ شَهِيدًۭا ثُمَّ لَا يُؤْذَنُ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ وَلَا هُمْ يُسْتَعْتَبُونَ
- 16:85 وَإِذَا رَءَا ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ ٱلْعَذَابَ فَلَا يُخَفَّفُ عَنْهُمْ وَلَا هُمْ يُنظَرُونَ
- 16:86 وَإِذَا رَءَا ٱلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا۟ شُرَكَآءَهُمْ قَالُوا۟ رَبَّنَا هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ شُرَكَآؤُنَا ٱلَّذِينَ كُنَّا نَدْعُوا۟ مِن دُونِكَ ۖ فَأَلْقَوْا۟ إِلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقَوْلَ إِنَّكُمْ لَكَٰذِبُونَ
- 16:87 وَأَلْقَوْا۟ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ يَوْمَئِذٍ ٱلسَّلَمَ ۖ وَضَلَّ عَنْهُم مَّا كَانُوا۟ يَفْتَرُونَ
- 16:88 ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ وَصَدُّوا۟ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ زِدْنَٰهُمْ عَذَابًۭا فَوْقَ ٱلْعَذَابِ بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يُفْسِدُونَ
- 16:89 وَيَوْمَ نَبْعَثُ فِى كُلِّ أُمَّةٍۢ شَهِيدًا عَلَيْهِم مِّنْ أَنفُسِهِمْ ۖ وَجِئْنَا بِكَ شَهِيدًا عَلَىٰ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ ۚ وَنَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ تِبْيَٰنًۭا لِّكُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ وَهُدًۭى وَرَحْمَةًۭ وَبُشْرَىٰ لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ
- 16:90 ۞ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأْمُرُ بِٱلْعَدْلِ وَٱلْإِحْسَٰنِ وَإِيتَآئِ ذِى ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ وَيَنْهَىٰ عَنِ ٱلْفَحْشَآءِ وَٱلْمُنكَرِ وَٱلْبَغْىِ ۚ يَعِظُكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ
- 16:91 وَأَوْفُوا۟ بِعَهْدِ ٱللَّهِ إِذَا عَٰهَدتُّمْ وَلَا تَنقُضُوا۟ ٱلْأَيْمَٰنَ بَعْدَ تَوْكِيدِهَا وَقَدْ جَعَلْتُمُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَيْكُمْ كَفِيلًا ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا تَفْعَلُونَ
- 16:92 وَلَا تَكُونُوا۟ كَٱلَّتِى نَقَضَتْ غَزْلَهَا مِنۢ بَعْدِ قُوَّةٍ أَنكَٰثًۭا تَتَّخِذُونَ أَيْمَٰنَكُمْ دَخَلًۢا بَيْنَكُمْ أَن تَكُونَ أُمَّةٌ هِىَ أَرْبَىٰ مِنْ أُمَّةٍ ۚ إِنَّمَا يَبْلُوكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِهِۦ ۚ وَلَيُبَيِّنَنَّ لَكُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ مَا كُنتُمْ فِيهِ تَخْتَلِفُونَ
- 16:93 وَلَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَجَعَلَكُمْ أُمَّةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ وَلَٰكِن يُضِلُّ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهْدِى مَن يَشَآءُ ۚ وَلَتُسْـَٔلُنَّ عَمَّا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
- 16:94 وَلَا تَتَّخِذُوٓا۟ أَيْمَٰنَكُمْ دَخَلًۢا بَيْنَكُمْ فَتَزِلَّ قَدَمٌۢ بَعْدَ ثُبُوتِهَا وَتَذُوقُوا۟ ٱلسُّوٓءَ بِمَا صَدَدتُّمْ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ وَلَكُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌۭ
- 16:95 وَلَا تَشْتَرُوا۟ بِعَهْدِ ٱللَّهِ ثَمَنًۭا قَلِيلًا ۚ إِنَّمَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ هُوَ خَيْرٌۭ لَّكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ
- 16:96 مَا عِندَكُمْ يَنفَدُ ۖ وَمَا عِندَ ٱللَّهِ بَاقٍۢ ۗ وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ صَبَرُوٓا۟ أَجْرَهُم بِأَحْسَنِ مَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ
- 16:97 مَنْ عَمِلَ صَٰلِحًۭا مِّن ذَكَرٍ أَوْ أُنثَىٰ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌۭ فَلَنُحْيِيَنَّهُۥ حَيَوٰةًۭ طَيِّبَةًۭ ۖ وَلَنَجْزِيَنَّهُمْ أَجْرَهُم بِأَحْسَنِ مَا كَانُوا۟ يَعْمَلُونَ
- 16:98 فَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ ٱلْقُرْءَانَ فَٱسْتَعِذْ بِٱللَّهِ مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ
- 16:99 إِنَّهُۥ لَيْسَ لَهُۥ سُلْطَٰنٌ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَعَلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ
- 16:100 إِنَّمَا سُلْطَٰنُهُۥ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ هُم بِهِۦ مُشْرِكُونَ
- 16:101 وَإِذَا بَدَّلْنَآ ءَايَةًۭ مَّكَانَ ءَايَةٍۢ ۙ وَٱللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا يُنَزِّلُ قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مُفْتَرٍۭ ۚ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
- 16:102 قُلْ نَزَّلَهُۥ رُوحُ ٱلْقُدُسِ مِن رَّبِّكَ بِٱلْحَقِّ لِيُثَبِّتَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَهُدًۭى وَبُشْرَىٰ لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ
- 16:103 وَلَقَدْ نَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُمْ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّمَا يُعَلِّمُهُۥ بَشَرٌۭ ۗ لِّسَانُ ٱلَّذِى يُلْحِدُونَ إِلَيْهِ أَعْجَمِىٌّۭ وَهَٰذَا لِسَانٌ عَرَبِىٌّۭ مُّبِينٌ
- 16:104 إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ لَا يَهْدِيهِمُ ٱللَّهُ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ
- 16:105 إِنَّمَا يَفْتَرِى ٱلْكَذِبَ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ وَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْكَٰذِبُونَ
- 16:106 مَن كَفَرَ بِٱللَّهِ مِنۢ بَعْدِ إِيمَٰنِهِۦٓ إِلَّا مَنْ أُكْرِهَ وَقَلْبُهُۥ مُطْمَئِنٌّۢ بِٱلْإِيمَٰنِ وَلَٰكِن مَّن شَرَحَ بِٱلْكُفْرِ صَدْرًۭا فَعَلَيْهِمْ غَضَبٌۭ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌۭ
- 16:107 ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمُ ٱسْتَحَبُّوا۟ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا عَلَى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ وَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِى ٱلْقَوْمَ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ
- 16:108 أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ طَبَعَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ وَسَمْعِهِمْ وَأَبْصَٰرِهِمْ ۖ وَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْغَٰفِلُونَ
- 16:109 لَا جَرَمَ أَنَّهُمْ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ هُمُ ٱلْخَٰسِرُونَ
- 16:110 ثُمَّ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لِلَّذِينَ هَاجَرُوا۟ مِنۢ بَعْدِ مَا فُتِنُوا۟ ثُمَّ جَٰهَدُوا۟ وَصَبَرُوٓا۟ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ مِنۢ بَعْدِهَا لَغَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ
- 16:111 ۞ يَوْمَ تَأْتِى كُلُّ نَفْسٍۢ تُجَٰدِلُ عَن نَّفْسِهَا وَتُوَفَّىٰ كُلُّ نَفْسٍۢ مَّا عَمِلَتْ وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ
- 16:112 وَضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلًۭا قَرْيَةًۭ كَانَتْ ءَامِنَةًۭ مُّطْمَئِنَّةًۭ يَأْتِيهَا رِزْقُهَا رَغَدًۭا مِّن كُلِّ مَكَانٍۢ فَكَفَرَتْ بِأَنْعُمِ ٱللَّهِ فَأَذَٰقَهَا ٱللَّهُ لِبَاسَ ٱلْجُوعِ وَٱلْخَوْفِ بِمَا كَانُوا۟ يَصْنَعُونَ
- 16:113 وَلَقَدْ جَآءَهُمْ رَسُولٌۭ مِّنْهُمْ فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأَخَذَهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ وَهُمْ ظَٰلِمُونَ
- 16:114 فَكُلُوا۟ مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ حَلَٰلًۭا طَيِّبًۭا وَٱشْكُرُوا۟ نِعْمَتَ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمْ إِيَّاهُ تَعْبُدُونَ
- 16:115 إِنَّمَا حَرَّمَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْمَيْتَةَ وَٱلدَّمَ وَلَحْمَ ٱلْخِنزِيرِ وَمَآ أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ ٱللَّهِ بِهِۦ ۖ فَمَنِ ٱضْطُرَّ غَيْرَ بَاغٍۢ وَلَا عَادٍۢ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌۭ
- 16:116 وَلَا تَقُولُوا۟ لِمَا تَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُكُمُ ٱلْكَذِبَ هَٰذَا حَلَٰلٌۭ وَهَٰذَا حَرَامٌۭ لِّتَفْتَرُوا۟ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلْكَذِبَ ۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَفْتَرُونَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ ٱلْكَذِبَ لَا يُفْلِحُونَ
- 16:117 مَتَٰعٌۭ قَلِيلٌۭ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌۭ
- 16:118 وَعَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُوا۟ حَرَّمْنَا مَا قَصَصْنَا عَلَيْكَ مِن قَبْلُ ۖ وَمَا ظَلَمْنَٰهُمْ وَلَٰكِن كَانُوٓا۟ أَنفُسَهُمْ يَظْلِمُونَ
- 16:119 ثُمَّ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لِلَّذِينَ عَمِلُوا۟ ٱلسُّوٓءَ بِجَهَٰلَةٍۢ ثُمَّ تَابُوا۟ مِنۢ بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ وَأَصْلَحُوٓا۟ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ مِنۢ بَعْدِهَا لَغَفُورٌۭ رَّحِيمٌ
- 16:120 إِنَّ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ كَانَ أُمَّةًۭ قَانِتًۭا لِّلَّهِ حَنِيفًۭا وَلَمْ يَكُ مِنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ
- 16:121 شَاكِرًۭا لِّأَنْعُمِهِ ۚ ٱجْتَبَىٰهُ وَهَدَىٰهُ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍۢ مُّسْتَقِيمٍۢ
- 16:122 وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُ فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةًۭ ۖ وَإِنَّهُۥ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ لَمِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
- 16:123 ثُمَّ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ أَنِ ٱتَّبِعْ مِلَّةَ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ حَنِيفًۭا ۖ وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ
- 16:124 إِنَّمَا جُعِلَ ٱلسَّبْتُ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ ٱخْتَلَفُوا۟ فِيهِ ۚ وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَيَحْكُمُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ فِيمَا كَانُوا۟ فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ
- 16:125 ٱدْعُ إِلَىٰ سَبِيلِ رَبِّكَ بِٱلْحِكْمَةِ وَٱلْمَوْعِظَةِ ٱلْحَسَنَةِ ۖ وَجَٰدِلْهُم بِٱلَّتِى هِىَ أَحْسَنُ ۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَن ضَلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦ ۖ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِٱلْمُهْتَدِينَ
- 16:126 وَإِنْ عَاقَبْتُمْ فَعَاقِبُوا۟ بِمِثْلِ مَا عُوقِبْتُم بِهِۦ ۖ وَلَئِن صَبَرْتُمْ لَهُوَ خَيْرٌۭ لِّلصَّٰبِرِينَ
- 16:127 وَٱصْبِرْ وَمَا صَبْرُكَ إِلَّا بِٱللَّهِ ۚ وَلَا تَحْزَنْ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا تَكُ فِى ضَيْقٍۢ مِّمَّا يَمْكُرُونَ
- 16:128 إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مَعَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوا۟ وَّٱلَّذِينَ هُم مُّحْسِنُونَ


===== _commentary/v16/work/s016/surah.r2/dictionary.md =====
# Dictionary: every branch of every focus root

Every root of the surah's words, each once, headed by the ayah and word where it first occurs; it also serves the later words listed with it.
One entry per branch: a Turkish label and Turkish glosses of its attested senses, then the classical dictionaries' own phrases with their source tags (ayn, sihah, tahdhib, maqayis, mufradat, jamhara). [kalıp] marks a sense the dictionaries attest only inside a fixed expression.
Identity roots come from the quran-data gateway. Word-scoped alternatives are cited analyses of this
exact word. **Echo roots** are observed but withheld mappings: sound-family candidates, not identity.

## ء ت ي (root_000009): 16:1 أَتَىٰٓ, 16:26 فَأَتَى, 16:26 وَأَتَىٰهُمُ, 16:27 أُوتُوا۟, 16:33 تَأْتِيَهُمُ, 16:33 يَأْتِىَ, 16:45 يَأْتِيَهُمُ, 16:55 ءَاتَيْنَٰهُمْ, 16:76 يَأْتِ, 16:90 وَإِيتَآئِ, 16:111 تَأْتِى, 16:112 يَأْتِيهَا, 16:122 وَءَاتَيْنَٰهُ

- **B001** gelmek, ulaşmak — gelmek veya ulaşmak · ona gitmek veya yanına varmak · geciktiğini düşünüp gelmesini istemek
  أتى يأتي أتيا (jamhara)؛ الإتيان المجئ (sihah)؛ أتاني فلان إتيانا وأتيا وأتية وأتوة (tahdhib;maqayis)؛ الإتيان مجيء بسهولة (mufradat)
- **B002** vermek; getirip sunmak — vermek; bir şeyi getirip sunmak
  آتى يؤتي إيتاء في معنى أعطى (jamhara)؛ آتاه إيتاء أي أعطاه وآتاه أيضا أي أتى به (sihah)؛ الإتياء الإعطاء (tahdhib)؛ الإيتاء الإعطاء (mufradat;maqayis)
- **B003** uygun yoldan ele almak ve elverişli hale gelmek — işin uygun yönü ve tutulacak yolu · uyma ve razı olma · bir şeyin ona elverişli hale gelmesi · ihtiyacını uygun yoldan ve incelikle yürütmek
  أتيت الأمر من مأتاته (sihah;maqayis)؛ آتيته على ذلك الأمر مواتاة إذا وافقته وطاوعته (sihah)؛ آتيت فلانا على أمره مؤاتاة وهو حسن المطاوعة (maqayis)؛ تأتى له الشيء أي تهيأ (sihah)؛ تأتى فلان لحاجته إذا ترفق لها (tahdhib)
- **B004** su kanalı açmak ve akışı yönlendirmek — su kanalı; suyu tutan odun ve yaprak birikintisi · bu suya yol açıp akışını yönlendirmek
  أت لمائك أي سهل له سبيلا وذلك السبيل الأتي (jamhara)؛ الأتي الجدول يؤتيه الرجل إلى أرضه (sihah)؛ كل جدول ماء أتي (tahdhib)؛ أت لهذا الماء أي سهل جريه (maqayis)؛ الأتي ما وقع في النهر من خشب أو ورق مما يحبس الماء (maqayis)
- **B005** başka bölgeden gelen sel [kalıp] — yağmur alan başka bir bölgeden gelen sel
  الأتي السيل بعينه يأتيك من بلد مطر من غير بلدك (jamhara)؛ سيل أتي وأتاوي إذا جاءك ولم يصبك مطره (sihah)؛ المسيل الذي يأتي من بلد قد مطر فيه إلى بلد لم يمطر فيه أتي (tahdhib)؛ السيل المار على وجهه أتي وأتاوي (mufradat)؛ الأتي أيضا السيل الذي يأتي من بلد غير بلدك (maqayis)
- **B006** topluluğa yabancı kimse [kalıp] — içinde bulunduğu topluluğa mensup olmayan yabancı adam
  رجل أتي وأتاوي وهو الغريب (jamhara)؛ الاتي أيضا والاتاوى الغريب (sihah)؛ إنما هو أتي فينا (tahdhib)؛ به شبه الغريب فقيل أتاوي (mufradat)؛ رجل أتي أي غريب في قوم ليس منهم وأتاوي كذلك (maqayis)
- **B007** gelişip bol ürün vermek — ekin ve hurmanın gelişmesi, ürünü ve bol verimi · çalkalanan tulumun yağının ortaya çıkması

  جئت على حزة منكرة أي حال وساعة (maqayis)؛ حزه حزة منكرة وليس هذا موضعه (jamhara)؛ الحز الحين والوقت (sihah)؛ الحزة الساعة أي حزة أتيتني (tahdhib)؛ الحز الوقت والحين (tahdhib)

- **B009** enine boyuna araştırma — enine boyuna araştırma
  المحازة الاستقصاء (tahdhib)

## ض ي ق (root_000925): 16:127 ضَيْقٍ

  خلاف السعة (maqayis;mufradat); ضاق الأمر يضيق ضيقا فهو ضيق (ayn;tahdhib); ضاق الشيء يضيق ضيقا (sihah); مكان ضيق وضيق (tahdhib); ضيقت عليك الموضع (sihah)

# s016 Semantic Channel Discovery

## Parent Channels

### 1. P1 16:1-18 - Directed Passage Through Marked Media
- Semantic invariant: Movement becomes reliable when a traversable medium is aligned, marked, and placed under purposeful control.
- Surface relation: direct; the straight and deviating way appears at 16:9, terrestrial paths and stellar guidance at 16:15-16, and the sea passage at 16:14.
- Surprising reach: The same navigational invariant extends from moral direction to road grooves, visible marks, a ship cutting water, and an anchor arresting drift.

#### Subchannel A. Straight road, deviating road, and tracked course
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A traveler enters a laid-out road, distinguishes its straight course from deviation, and follows it by guidance.
- Active motifs: extended road `quranic:root_000672:B001/m01`; straight road-walking `quranic:root_001230:B002/m01`; deviation from aim and justice `quranic:root_000275:B001/m01`; road grooves `quranic:root_000791:B005/m01`; gentle direction to road and truth `quranic:root_001583:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `س ب ل` 16:9, 15; `ق ص د`, `ج و ر` 16:9; `ش ر ك` 16:1, 3; `ه د ي` 16:9, 15-16
- Synthesis: The surface contrast between a purposeful way and a deviating one becomes a concrete track scene. A road has an extended course and grooves, while guidance is the act that keeps the traveler aligned with it.

#### Subchannel B. Waymarks that convert visibility into direction
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Distinct visible marks and rising stars identify position and guide a moving observer.
- Active motifs: distinguishing landmark `quranic:root_001040:B002/m01`; rising star `quranic:root_001475:B001/m01`; visible sign `quranic:root_000074:B003/m01`; waymark or appointed marker `quranic:root_000051:B005/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `ع ل م` 16:8, 16; `ن ج م` 16:12, 16; `ء ي ي` 16:11-13; `ء م ر` 16:1-2, 12
- Synthesis: Signs are not merely proofs in this scene; they are discriminating marks. The star is one elevated instance of a broader semiotic apparatus in which a visible trace makes direction recoverable.

#### Subchannel C. Vessel cleaving a controlled waterway
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A ship enters broad water, is driven through it, cuts a sounding course, and can be arrested at an anchorage.
- Active motifs: ship circulating on water `quranic:root_001177:B003/m01`; ship cleaving water `quranic:root_001405:B001/m01`; broad abundant water `quranic:root_000086:B001/m01`; purposeful subjection and steering `quranic:root_000685:B001/m01`; ship at anchor `quranic:root_000564:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `ف ل ك`, `م خ ر`, `ب ح ر` 16:14; `س خ ر` 16:12, 14; `ر س و` 16:15
- Synthesis: The sea is rendered as a navigable medium rather than an undifferentiated expanse. Subjection supplies controlled motion, the prow materializes passage as a cut in water, and anchoring supplies the complementary operation of stopping.

### 2. P1 16:1-18 - Fluid Inputs Becoming Living Yield
- Semantic invariant: A small or descending fluid enters a receptive interior or substrate and emerges as organized life, growth, or fruit.
- Surface relation: direct; human creation from a drop occurs at 16:4, and descending water producing crops and fruit at 16:10-11.
- Surprising reach: Human gestation and agricultural germination form parallel transformation mechanisms, with semen figured as seed and fruit as an internally carried yield.

#### Subchannel A. Generative drop, womb, and concealed burden
- Reading type: latent/lexical
- Scene or process: Generative fluid is placed in a womb-like interior, carried out of sight, and formed into created life.
- Active motifs: semen-bearing water-drop `quranic:root_001518:B002/m01`; origination of a created being `quranic:root_000434:B002/m01`; female womb `quranic:root_000552:B003/m01`; concealed gestational burden `quranic:root_000357:B002/m01`; semen figured as seed `quranic:root_000630:B004/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `ن ط ف` 16:4; `خ ل ق` 16:3-5, 8, 17; `ر ح م` 16:7, 18; `ح م ل` 16:7; `ز ر ع` 16:11
- Synthesis: The drop of 16:4 opens a latent reproductive mechanism distributed across local roots. Fluid becomes seed, the womb receives it, carrying preserves the hidden process, and creation names the formed outcome.

#### Subchannel B. Delivered water, germination, and ripened output
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Water is delivered to the ground, enters irrigation channels, raises vegetation, and terminates in crop and fruit.
- Active motifs: downward delivery `quranic:root_001492:B002/m01`; water conveyed by irrigation or pouring `quranic:root_001458:B003/m01`; vegetation emerging from earth `quranic:root_001465:B001/m01`; crop cultivation and growth `quranic:root_000630:B001/m01`; ripened fruit `quranic:root_000205:B001/m01`; edible crop yield `quranic:root_000043:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `ن ز ل` 16:2, 10; `م و ه` 16:10; `ن ب ت`, `ز ر ع`, `ث م ر` 16:11; `ء ك ل` 16:5, 14
- Synthesis: The rain sequence is a material production chain. Delivery and irrigation are distinct operations, germination is the transition into life, and crop, fruit, and edible yield are successive outcomes rather than a single provision bucket.

### 3. P1 16:1-18 - The Herd as a Provision and Transport System
- Semantic invariant: Domesticated animals convert managed movement and embodied capacity into food, warmth, and carriage.
- Surface relation: direct; 16:5-8 presents livestock as sources of warmth, benefit, food, beauty, load-bearing, and riding.
- Surprising reach: The pastoral cycle and the freight journey separate into two mechanisms: recurrent release and return at pasture, and one-way transfer of a heavy load toward a distant destination.

#### Subchannel A. Release to pasture and return with usable yield
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Herd animals are released to graze, return at evening, and supply warmth and recurring benefits.
- Active motifs: livestock wealth `quranic:root_001525:B005/m01`; warmth and produce of camels `quranic:root_000479:B002/m01`; grazing herd `quranic:root_000694:B005/m01`; free ranging in pasture `quranic:root_000764:B003/m01`; evening return of livestock `quranic:root_000609:B005/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `ن ع م` 16:5, 18; `د ف ء` 16:5; `س ر ح`, `ر و ح` 16:6; `س و م` 16:10
- Synthesis: The animals participate in a repeated husbandry cycle: outward release, feeding, and homeward return. Warmth and other benefits are outputs of that managed circulation, not isolated attributes.

#### Subchannel B. Load, mount, destination, and bodily strain
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A carrier takes up weight, bears it on a mount, and reaches a destination that would otherwise exact severe effort.
- Active motifs: lifting and bearing an external load `quranic:root_000357:B001/m01`; physical heaviness `quranic:root_000202:B001/m01`; riding on an animal's back `quranic:root_000589:B001/m01`; arrival at the goal `quranic:root_000151:B001/m01`; burden that splits or strains the self `quranic:root_000807:B003/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `ح م ل`, `ث ق ل`, `ب ل غ`, `ش ق ق` 16:7; `ر ك ب` 16:8
- Synthesis: This is a freight mechanism with distinct roles: weight, bearer, mounted support, destination, and strain avoided. The lexical image of something that splits the self gives bodily force to the counterfactual hardship in 16:7.

### 4. P1 16:1-18 - Stabilized Orders Above and Below
- Semantic invariant: Potentially moving domains are fixed, regulated, or subjected so that human life can occupy a stable world.
- Surface relation: direct; celestial bodies are subjected at 16:12, while mountains, rivers, and paths stabilize and articulate the earth at 16:15.
- Surprising reach: Geological anchoring and celestial scheduling are parallel control systems, one arresting lateral sway and the other regularizing cyclical passage.

#### Subchannel A. Anchored ground and opened watercourse
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A fixed mass arrests ground movement while a river cuts an open channel across the stabilized surface.
- Active motifs: fixed and rooted mass `quranic:root_000564:B001/m01`; swaying disturbance `quranic:root_001459:B001/m01`; lower ground opposite the sky `quranic:root_000025:B001/m01`; river cleaving earth with running water `quranic:root_001559:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `ر س و`, `م ي د`, `ء ر ض`, `ن ه ر` 16:15
- Synthesis: Mountain and river perform complementary operations. One fixes the substrate against oscillation; the other opens a stable line of flow through it.

#### Subchannel B. Regulated alternation of luminous bodies
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Night and daylight alternate while sun, moon, and stars move under a governing command.
- Active motifs: purposeful subjection `quranic:root_000685:B001/m01`; night and its darkness `quranic:root_001392:B001/m01`; daylight opening in brightness `quranic:root_001559:B002/m01`; sun `quranic:root_000818:B001/m01`; moon and its light `quranic:root_001255:B001/m01`; rising star `quranic:root_001475:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `س خ ر`, `ل ي ل`, `ن ه ر`, `ش م س`, `ق م ر`, `ن ج م` 16:12; `ن ج م` also 16:16
- Synthesis: Subjection is expressed as regulated recurrence rather than static possession. Darkness opens into day while luminous bodies retain distinct roles inside one ordered cycle.

### 5. P2 16:19-36 - Liability Carried to Completion
- Semantic invariant: Wrong action becomes a transferable but fully accounted load whose settlement reaches both deed and bearer.
- Surface relation: direct; full burdens are carried at 16:25, souls are taken and deeds recompensed at 16:28, 32, and the results of action close around perpetrators at 16:34.
- Surprising reach: Moral liability is materialized as freight, while completion vocabulary links the total load to full payment and the taking of the person who bears it.

#### Subchannel A. Own load plus induced load
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A bearer takes up a complete burden and adds liability generated by leading others away.
- Active motifs: bearing an entrusted or culpable load `quranic:root_000357:B003/m01`; heavy burden `quranic:root_001643:B002/m01`; completion without deficiency `quranic:root_001318:B001/m01`; straying from guidance and aim `quranic:root_000913:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `ح م ل`, `و ز ر`, `ك م ل`, `ض ل ل` 16:25; `ض ل ل` also 16:36
- Synthesis: The load is not merely accumulated; it has provenance. One portion belongs to the bearer's own action and another arises from induced deviation, yet the total is carried without reduction.

#### Subchannel B. Complete taking and recompense
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: The account is brought to fullness, the soul is taken, and intended action receives its matching return.
- Active motifs: full settlement `quranic:root_001669:B001/m01`; taking the soul in death `quranic:root_001669:B002/m01`; intentional deed `quranic:root_001046:B001/m01`; recompense matching action `quranic:root_000244:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `و ف ي` 16:28, 32; `ع م ل` 16:28, 32, 34; `ج ز ي` 16:31
- Synthesis: Completion governs both sides of the settlement: nothing is missing from what is taken, and nothing is missing from what is repaid. The same mechanism joins death, deed, and recompense without collapsing them into one event.

### 6. P2 16:19-36 - Built Destinations That Collapse or Receive
- Semantic invariant: Humanly inhabited structures disclose their quality through what happens at their boundaries and supports.
- Surface relation: direct; a foundation-and-roof structure collapses at 16:26, while gates, dwellings, gardens, and flowing rivers receive their occupants at 16:29-32.
- Surprising reach: Judgment is spatially engineered as two opposed architectural sequences: failure propagating upward from foundations, and stable entry propagating inward through a gate.

#### Subchannel A. Foundation failure and descending roof
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A built support fails at its base, the upper covering falls, and harm encloses occupants from an unanticipated direction.
- Active motifs: construction by joining parts `quranic:root_000156:B001/m01`; foundations and supporting bases `quranic:root_001244:B007/m01`; high roof `quranic:root_000720:B001/m01`; noisy collapsing fall `quranic:root_000402:B001/m01`; harm descending and enclosing `quranic:root_000381:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `ب ن ي`, `ق ع د`, `س ق ف`, `خ ر ر` 16:26; `ح ي ق` 16:34
- Synthesis: The scene separates support, covering, and failure. Collapse begins where stability should originate, then reverses the shelter's function as the roof becomes the vehicle of enclosure.

#### Subchannel B. Gate, entry, garden, and settled flow
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: An entrant passes a threshold into a planted, concealed dwelling whose water flows beneath it.
- Active motifs: entrance or gate `quranic:root_000163:B001/m01`; passage into an interior `quranic:root_000464:B001/m01`; stable lodging `quranic:root_000211:B001/m01`; tree-covered garden `quranic:root_000266:B003/m01`; running and streaming `quranic:root_000240:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `ب و ب` 16:29; `د خ ل` 16:29, 31-32; `ث و ي` 16:29; `ج ن ن`, `ج ر ي` 16:31
- Synthesis: Entry is a staged movement through boundary, interior, and settled residence. Vegetation conceals the dwelling while flowing water keeps the interior alive, opposing the failed enclosure of the preceding subchannel.

### 7. P2 16:19-36 - Hidden States Becoming Knowable
- Semantic invariant: What is inward, absent, or unperceived is exposed by a transition into visibility, awareness, or animation.
- Surface relation: direct; hidden and public acts are known at 16:19, and lifeless objects are contrasted with resurrection-awareness at 16:20-21.
- Surprising reach: Fine perception and the stirring of a dormant body make disclosure a change of state, not only an increase in information.

#### Subchannel A. Secret, public, and finely perceived
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A concealed act crosses into public visibility and is apprehended even at the level of subtle signs.
- Active motifs: concealment in the inward part `quranic:root_000697:B001/m01`; public manifestation `quranic:root_001041:B001/m01`; knowledge as disclosure to the knower `quranic:root_001040:B001/m01`; fine perception and subtle awareness `quranic:root_000798:B005/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `س ر ر`, `ع ل ن`, `ع ل م` 16:19, 23; `ش ع ر` 16:21, 26
- Synthesis: The secret/public opposition is completed by a perceiver capable of detecting what does not announce itself loudly. Knowledge therefore reaches from manifest declaration down to a fine trace.

#### Subchannel B. Dormancy stirred into awareness
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A lifeless state is contrasted with animated life, while resurrection is pictured as the stirring of what had lain still.
- Active motifs: loss of life and force `quranic:root_001454:B001/m01`; living animate being `quranic:root_000383:B003/m01`; stirring the dormant from rest `quranic:root_000129:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `م و ت`, `ح ي ي`, `ب ع ث` 16:21
- Synthesis: Resurrection acquires a kinetic image: stillness is not simply negated but actively disturbed. The latent stirring motif sharpens the surface contrast between dead objects and beings aware of being raised.

### 8. P2 16:19-36 - Sent Guidance and Traced Consequence
- Semantic invariant: Guidance is dispatched through an authorized messenger and then tested by following the historical route to its outcome.
- Surface relation: direct; messengers are sent to every community at 16:36, and hearers are told to travel the earth and inspect the deniers' end.
- Surprising reach: Message delivery and terrestrial travel form one relay: a directive moves outward through a messenger, while the recipient moves outward to read consequence in place.

#### Subchannel A. Dispatch, message, and clear delivery
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A messenger is raised and sent into a community to deliver an intelligible directive.
- Active motifs: dispatching an emissary `quranic:root_000129:B002/m01`; messenger and message `quranic:root_000563:B002/m01`; conveying a message to its destination `quranic:root_000151:B002/m01`; disclosure by speech or sign `quranic:root_000170:B005/m01`; community or people-type `quranic:root_000053:B004/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `ب ع ث`, `ر س ل` 16:36; `ب ل غ` 16:35; `ب ي ن` 16:35; `ء م م` 16:36
- Synthesis: The scene distinguishes sender, emissary, recipient collective, content, and successful delivery. Clarity is the condition that makes dispatch function as guidance rather than mere movement.

#### Subchannel B. Travel that reads an ending
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: An observer traverses the ground, inspects prior traces, and recognizes the terminal result of deviation.
- Active motifs: physical going and travel `quranic:root_000769:B001/m01`; way of life or conduct `quranic:root_000769:B002/m01`; ground as traversed lower domain `quranic:root_000025:B001/m01`; directed observation `quranic:root_001520:B001/m01`; terminal outcome `quranic:root_001033:B006/m01`; straying from the intended course `quranic:root_000913:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `س ي ر`, `ء ر ض`, `ن ظ ر`, `ع ق ب`, `ض ل ل` 16:36
- Synthesis: Travel and moral conduct are kept as separate senses of the same root: one is the observer's movement, the other the historical course under inspection. Their bridge is consequence, the point where a lived route becomes legible.

### 9. P3 16:37-50 - Word Moving from Intention to Effect
- Semantic invariant: An inwardly held directive becomes public and effective through speech, revelation, inscription, and explanation.
- Surface relation: direct; the creative command is enacted at 16:40, revelation is sent to human messengers at 16:43, and written proofs are explained at 16:44.
- Surprising reach: Hidden indication, inscribed text, spoken command, and realized event form successive media rather than interchangeable forms of "communication."

#### Subchannel A. Command that realizes its object
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Will resolves into a spoken directive, and the addressed state immediately comes into occurrence.
- Active motifs: articulated speech `quranic:root_001272:B001/m01`; binding directive `quranic:root_000051:B002/m01`; occurrence in time `quranic:root_001332:B001/m01`; will and intention `quranic:root_000610:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `ق و ل` 16:40; `ء م ر` 16:50; `ك و ن`, `ر و د` 16:40
- Synthesis: The scene preserves four roles: intention, command, addressed object, and realized state. Its force lies in the absence of an intervening production apparatus: the word itself completes the transition into occurrence.

#### Subchannel B. Hidden revelation opened by explanation
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: Divine information is transmitted in a hidden mode, fixed in a written medium, recalled, queried, and opened into explicit meaning.
- Active motifs: divine hidden communication `quranic:root_001633:B004/m01`; written book or inscription `quranic:root_000621:B003/m01`; reminder that restores attention `quranic:root_000516:B009/m01`; disclosure by speech or sign `quranic:root_000170:B005/m01`; directed request for knowledge `quranic:root_000661:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `و ح ي`, `س ء ل` 16:43; `ز ب ر`, `ذ ك ر`, `ب ي ن` 16:44
- Synthesis: Revelation begins as knowledge imparted beyond ordinary publicity, but it does not remain closed. Inscription preserves it, reminder reactivates it, questions approach qualified knowers, and explanation opens its semantic contents.

### 10. P3 16:37-50 - Relocation Secured by Patience and Trust
- Semantic invariant: Separation from a hostile place becomes a viable relocation when a new abode, sustained restraint, and delegated reliance hold the displaced person.
- Surface relation: direct; those who emigrate are settled well at 16:41, and their patience and trust are named at 16:42.
- Surprising reach: Reward also carries a lexical image of repairing a break, making settlement a mending operation after spatial rupture.

#### Subchannel A. Severance, movement, and new abode
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A person breaks from one dwelling, crosses distance, and is installed in a prepared place.
- Active motifs: severance and departure `quranic:root_001578:B001/m01`; movement from one abode to another `quranic:root_001578:B002/m01`; taking an abode `quranic:root_000162:B001/m01`; dwelling or station `quranic:root_001492:B003/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `ه ج ر`, `ب و ء` 16:41; `ن ز ل` 16:44
- Synthesis: Emigration is not reduced to departure. Severance creates a spatial deficit, movement crosses it, and emplacement in an abode supplies the missing terminal operation.

#### Subchannel B. Restraint, reliance, and repaired loss
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: The displaced person contains panic, entrusts the unsettled matter, and receives both recompense and repair.

### 11. P3 16:37-50 - Seizure Closing Vertical and Lateral Escape

- Reading type: mixed

#### Subchannel B. Capture during turning and attrition
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A target is taken while changing course or is diminished progressively until security disappears.
- Active motifs: turning a thing from its face `quranic:root_001248:B004/m01`; arrest and capture `quranic:root_000018:B003/m01`; subtractive taking from a thing `quranic:root_000447:B004/m01`; anticipatory fear `quranic:root_000447:B001/m01`

- Synthesis: Refuge is an enacted boundary. Recitation initiates it, invocation establishes the protective relation, expulsion moves the threat outside, and security names the resulting interior state.

### 22. P7 16:101-112 - Message Stabilized Through Substitution and Accusation
- Semantic invariant: A message can change its presented unit while preserving truthful direction through its source, medium, language, and reception.
- Surface relation: direct; verse substitution is named at 16:101, the Holy Spirit brings stabilizing truth at 16:102, and foreign-language and human-teacher accusations are answered at 16:103-105.
- Surprising reach: Replacement, descent, spiritual transmission, script disambiguation, linguistic clarity, and fabrication are distinct operations inside one contested transmission scene.

#### Subchannel A. One sign standing in place of another
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A sign is replaced by another under knowledgeable control, while opponents misdescribe the operation as fabrication.
- Active motifs: one thing standing in another's place `quranic:root_000095:B001/m01`; visible sign `quranic:root_000074:B003/m01`; downward delivery `quranic:root_001492:B002/m01`; knowledge as disclosed apprehension `quranic:root_001040:B001/m01`; saying what did not exist or falsely attributing it `quranic:root_001272:B005/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `ب د ل`, `ء ي ي`, `ن ز ل`, `ع ل م`, `ق و ل` 16:101
- Synthesis: Substitution changes position and sequence, not source knowledge. The accusation fails by confusing replacement within a controlled transmission with invention outside it.

#### Subchannel B. Spirit-delivered truth stabilizing the receiver
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A life-bearing spiritual agent carries truth downward, fixing the recipient's heart and directing belief.
- Active motifs: spirit that gives life to the body `quranic:root_000609:B001/m01`; downward delivery `quranic:root_001492:B002/m01`; firmness of heart, reason, and tongue `quranic:root_000192:B002/m01`; reality fixed against falsehood `quranic:root_000347:B001/m01`; trusting assent of the heart `quranic:root_000054:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `ر و ح`, `ن ز ل`, `ث ب ت`, `ح ق ق`, `ء م ن` 16:102
- Synthesis: The medium and effect mirror one another: a spirit associated with life delivers a truth associated with fixed reality, and the result is an inward stabilization rather than mere receipt of information.

#### Subchannel C. Clear language opened against foreign opacity
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: An allegedly opaque source-language is set against speech whose structure makes meaning explicit.
- Active motifs: language and speech-system `quranic:root_001355:B006/m01`; clear articulation `quranic:root_000996:B001/m01`; non-articulate or non-Arabic speech `quranic:root_000988:B001/m01`; removing script ambiguity by marking letters `quranic:root_000988:B002/m01`; disclosure by speech or sign `quranic:root_000170:B005/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `ل س ن`, `ع ر ب`, `ع ج م`, `ب ي ن` 16:103
- Synthesis: The contrast is not reduced to ethnic labels. Opacity concerns intelligibility, dotting concerns visual disambiguation, and clear articulation concerns the successful opening of meaning in a linguistic system.

#### Subchannel D. Human attribution turned into fabrication
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A human source is alleged, the statement bends away from its object, and repeated attribution hardens into a fabricated account.
- Active motifs: invented falsehood `quranic:root_001150:B003/m01`; falsehood opposed to truth `quranic:root_001290:B001/m01`; verbal deviation and objection `quranic:root_001345:B004/m01`; visible human being `quranic:root_000120:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `ب ش ر`, `ل ح د` 16:103; `ف ر ي` 16:101, 105; `ك ذ ب` 16:105
- Synthesis: The accusation is a social production scene: a visible human is assigned as source, language is bent to sustain the claim, and invention supplies content that the attribution cannot establish.

### 23. P7 16:101-112 - Inner Apertures Opened or Sealed
- Semantic invariant: The inward person is figured as a set of openings that can remain secure, expand toward a chosen object, or be closed against perception.
- Surface relation: direct; a secure heart under coercion is contrasted with a breast opened to unbelief at 16:106, and hearts, hearing, and sight are sealed at 16:108.
- Surprising reach: Coercion acts from outside, expansion acts from inside, and sealing acts at the sensory boundary, so outward conformity and inward state remain analytically distinct.

#### Subchannel A. Coerced exterior and secure heart
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: External force compels an act while the heart remains settled, opposite an interior that actively expands toward rejection.
- Active motifs: compelling another into what is disliked `quranic:root_001295:B003/m01`; inward heart `quranic:root_001248:B001/m01`; settled security `quranic:root_000054:B001/m01`; inward expansion of desire `quranic:root_000784:B005/m01`; chest as source of action `quranic:root_000849:B004/m01`; surging wrath `quranic:root_001092:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `ك ر ه`, `ق ل ب`, `ء م ن`, `ش ر ح`, `ص د ر`, `غ ض ب` 16:106
- Synthesis: The scene distinguishes pressure, assent, and consequence. Coercion reaches the exterior without necessarily reorganizing the heart, while opening the breast describes an internally welcomed orientation that exposes the person to wrath.

#### Subchannel B. Sensorium closed by a stamp
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A stamp closes the heart and perceptual organs, leaving the person outside alert reception.
- Active motifs: seal impressed by a stamp `quranic:root_000926:B001/m01`; inward heart `quranic:root_001248:B001/m01`; hearing sound `quranic:root_000741:B001/m01`; visual perception `quranic:root_000121:B001/m01`; inattentiveness that leaves something outside awareness `quranic:root_001097:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `ط ب ع`, `ق ل ب`, `س م ع`, `ب ص ر`, `غ ف ل` 16:108
- Synthesis: Sealing is a boundary operation, not a synonym for ignorance. It prevents entry through hearing and sight and closes the inward site that would integrate their input, producing heedlessness as the resulting state.

### 24. P7 16:101-112 - Civic Condition Worn and Tasted
- Semantic invariant: A community's security or deprivation is materialized as something that surrounds the body, fills or empties the belly, and is directly experienced.
- Surface relation: direct; 16:112 presents a secure, settled town with abundant provision that is made to taste a garment of hunger and fear.
- Surprising reach: Civic economy becomes multisensory: settlement is spatial, provision is nutritive, deprivation is clothing, and punishment is taste.

#### Subchannel A. Settled town receiving ample provision
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A gathered settlement remains calm and secure while sustenance reaches it in broad supply.
- Active motifs: people gathered in a town `quranic:root_001222:B001/m01`; settled security `quranic:root_000054:B001/m01`; calm after disturbance `quranic:root_003669:B001/m01`; nutritive provision `quranic:root_000560:B002/m01`; expansive ease of life `quranic:root_000576:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `ق ر ي`, `ء م ن`, `ط م ن`, `ر ز ق`, `ر غ د` 16:112
- Synthesis: Security, calm, and abundance occupy different roles. Security protects the boundary, calm characterizes the settlement's internal state, and provision supplies the continuing material flow that makes ease possible.

#### Subchannel B. Hunger and fear becoming garment and taste
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: An emptied belly and anticipatory fear envelop the community like clothing and become an experienced flavor.
- Active motifs: empty belly and hunger `quranic:root_000278:B001/m01`; anticipatory fear `quranic:root_000447:B001/m01`; covering by clothing `quranic:root_001341:B001/m01`; literal tasting `quranic:root_000526:B001/m01`; experiential testing `quranic:root_000526:B002/m01`; produced deed `quranic:root_000885:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `ج و ع`, `خ و ف`, `ل ب س`, `ذ و ق`, `ص ن ع` 16:112
- Synthesis: Deprivation reaches the community through several bodily interfaces. Hunger hollows the inside, fear anticipates what comes next, clothing surrounds the outside, and taste converts the whole condition into immediate experience tied to what was made.

### 25. P8 16:113-128 - Food Boundaries and Their Classification
- Semantic invariant: A consumable is governed by boundaries that may be released, imposed, crossed under necessity, falsely named, or narrated through precedent.
- Surface relation: direct; lawful good food and specified prohibitions appear at 16:114-115, false lawful-unlawful labels at 16:116, and prior Jewish restrictions at 16:118.
- Surprising reach: Legal classification is rendered through knot release, barrier crossing, tongue-made labels, and narrated precedent.

#### Subchannel A. Releasing a prohibition around good food
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A binding restriction is loosened so wholesome provision may pass into consumption.
- Active motifs: untying a knot `quranic:root_000351:B001/m01`; removal of a prohibition `quranic:root_000351:B003/m01`; forbidding and barring `quranic:root_000313:B001/m01`; wholesome quality `quranic:root_000961:B001/m01`; eating food `quranic:root_000043:B001/m01`; nutritive provision `quranic:root_000560:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `ح ل ل` 16:114, 116; `ح ر م` 16:115-116; `ط ي ب`, `ء ك ل`, `ر ز ق` 16:114
- Synthesis: Lawfulness is a boundary operation with a concrete lexical mechanics: what had been tied or barred is released. Wholesomeness describes the admitted object, eating the bodily passage, and provision its sustaining function.

#### Subchannel B. Necessity crossing without transgression
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A constrained person crosses a food boundary only as far as bodily necessity requires, without converting exception into aggression.
- Active motifs: compelling necessity `quranic:root_000907:B003/m01`; exceeding a limit through aggression `quranic:root_000138:B003/m01`; crossing the boundary in wrongdoing `quranic:root_000993:B001/m01`; covering a sin and its effect `quranic:root_001096:B002/m01`; merciful tenderness `quranic:root_000552:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `ض ر ر`, `ب غ ي`, `ع د و`, `غ ف ر`, `ر ح م` 16:115
- Synthesis: Exception is calibrated by distance traveled across the boundary. Necessity supplies the pressure, aggression names excess motion, and forgiveness and mercy protect the constrained actor whose crossing stops at need.

#### Subchannel C. Tongue manufacturing lawful and unlawful labels
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A tongue composes a description, falsely attaches a legal predicate, and circulates the invention as authoritative classification.
- Active motifs: tongue as speech organ `quranic:root_001355:B001/m01`; presenting a thing by attributed qualities `quranic:root_001654:B001/m01`; saying what did not exist or falsely attributing it `quranic:root_001272:B005/m01`; falsehood opposed to truth `quranic:root_001290:B001/m01`; invented falsehood `quranic:root_001150:B003/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `ل س ن`, `و ص ف`, `ق و ل`, `ك ذ ب`, `ف ر ي` 16:116
- Synthesis: The legal error is produced in stages: articulation, description, attachment of a predicate, and fabrication. This keeps false classification distinct from the genuine boundary operations of release and prohibition.

#### Subchannel D. Narrated restriction and self-misplacement
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A prior community receives restrictions, its history is carried forward in narration, and wrongful action displaces responsibility onto the actors themselves.
- Active motifs: Jewish communal identity `quranic:root_001605:B002/m01`; forbidding and barring `quranic:root_000313:B001/m01`; sequential narration `quranic:root_001232:B002/m01`; placing a thing in the wrong position `quranic:root_000967:B004/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `ه و د`, `ح ر م`, `ق ص ص`, `ظ ل م` 16:118
- Synthesis: Precedent is not a static list. Narration preserves who received the restriction, while the lexical image of misplacement materializes how wrongful action returns liability to the community rather than to the giver of the rule.

- Synthesis: Following is both relational and spatial. Tracking preserves proximity to the exemplar, repeated passage marks the creed as a traversable course, upright inclination fixes orientation, and guidance maintains the line.

#### Subchannel B. A selected person functioning as community and model
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: One obedient person gathers the functions of origin, community, gratitude, and selected exemplar.

- Synthesis: The individual is enlarged without ceasing to be an individual. As origin he gathers reference, as community he gathers social function, as obedient and grateful actor he supplies repeatable conduct, and selection establishes his exemplary standing.

### 27. P8 16:113-128 - Calibrated Response Under Conflict
- Semantic invariant: Speech, penalty, and inward affect remain just when response is held to an appropriate form and measure.
- Surface relation: direct; invitation and best argument appear at 16:125, equivalent retaliation and patience at 16:126, and restraint from grief and constriction at 16:127.
- Surprising reach: Argument is an intertwining of strands, retaliation is a measured return, and patience is an internal holding operation shared across discourse, action, and affect.

#### Subchannel A. Invitation, wisdom, admonition, and entwined dispute
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A caller draws an interlocutor toward a path through fitting knowledge, affective reminder, and disciplined exchange.
- Active motifs: calling and drawing by speech `quranic:root_000478:B001/m01`; accurate practical wisdom `quranic:root_000348:B003/m01`; fear-tinged reminder that softens the heart `quranic:root_001663:B001/m01`; intertwined dispute `quranic:root_000229:B002/m01`; good form opposed to ugliness `quranic:root_000323:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `د ع و`, `ح ك م`, `و ع ظ`, `ج د ل`, `ح س ن` 16:125
- Synthesis: The discourse scene assigns different work to each instrument. Invitation establishes direction, wisdom fits the approach, admonition reaches affect, and argument engages resistance without allowing the strands of dispute to become disorder.

#### Subchannel B. Retaliation held to equivalent measure
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: An injury is answered by a matching return, while patience can interrupt the retaliatory sequence.
- Active motifs: punishment following offense `quranic:root_001033:B007/m01`; equivalence and counterpart `quranic:root_001397:B001/m01`; holding the self from panic `quranic:root_000840:B001/m01`; exact retaliatory redress `quranic:root_000840:B012/m01`; beneficial superiority `quranic:root_000452:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `ع ق ب`, `م ث ل`, `ص ب ر`, `خ ي ر` 16:126
- Synthesis: Retaliation is not unrestricted counterforce; equivalence sets its magnitude. The distinct patience sense then supplies a real alternative operation, withholding the self from continuing the return and thereby opening the better outcome.

#### Subchannel C. Grief and constriction held inside bounds
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: The self contains grief and resists narrowing into a constricted inward state.
- Active motifs: holding the self from panic `quranic:root_000840:B001/m01`; roughness of the self through grief `quranic:root_000317:B001/m01`; constriction of the chest `quranic:root_000925:B002/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `ص ب ر`, `ح ز ن`, `ض ي ق` 16:127
- Synthesis: Patience here is neither argument nor retaliation but affective containment. Grief roughens the inward surface and constriction narrows it; restraint prevents those states from determining the actor's course.

### S1. P1 16:1-18 - Counting Pebbles Against Uncontained Blessing
- Reading type: mixed
- Scene or process: A counter handles discrete units and seeks exhaustive enumeration, but the benefaction exceeds the counting apparatus and is met by protective covering.
- Active motifs: counted number `quranic:root_000989:B001/m01`; pebble as a countable object `quranic:root_000332:B001/m01`; exhaustive enumeration `quranic:root_000332:B002/m01`; good condition and blessing `quranic:root_001525:B001/m01`; protective covering `quranic:root_001096:B001/m01`; merciful tenderness `quranic:root_000552:B001/m01`
- Ayah anchors: `ع د د`, `ح ص ي`, `ن ع م`, `غ ف ر`, `ر ح م` 16:18
- Synthesis: Enumeration is materialized through the pebble, an object naturally handled one by one. The scene presses that finite technique against an uncontainable field of blessing, while covering and mercy answer the inevitable remainder left outside the count.

### S2. P2 16:19-36 - Ancestral Script as a Fabricated Record

- Ayah anchors: `س ط ر`, `ء و ل`, `ق و ل` 16:24; `ك ذ ب` 16:36
